title: Harees (slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge)

ingredients.name: cracked wheat (or pearled wheat berries), soaked overnight
lamb or chicken on the bone

steps: Drain the soaked wheat and rinse it well.
Put the meat, onion, cardamom, cinnamon stick and water in a large pot, bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add the wheat and salt, then cover and simmer on very low heat for 2 to 3 hours, stirring from time to time, until the meat is falling off the bone and the wheat is very soft.
Remove the bones, cinnamon stick and onion and shred the meat back into the pot.
Beat the mixture vigorously with a wooden spoon or a masher for several minutes until it turns into a thick, smooth, sticky porridge. Add hot water if it is too stiff.
Spread the harees in a shallow bowl, make a hollow in the middle, pour in the hot ghee and dust with ground cinnamon.

title: Hininy (Najdi date and bread dessert)

ingredients.name: brown or whole-wheat bread, crumbled (or toasted whole-wheat flour)
saffron threads soaked in 1 tbsp warm water

steps: Toast the crumbled bread in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, for about 5 minutes until it is dry and lightly golden, then set aside.
Mash the dates with the warm water into a thick paste, using a fork or a food processor.
Melt the ghee in a pan, add the date paste and stir over low heat for about 5 minutes until it softens and loosens.
Stir in the toasted bread, the cardamom and the saffron with its soaking water. Keep stirring until everything forms a thick, sticky, evenly mixed mass.
Press it into a shallow dish and smooth the top, or serve it warm, heaped into small bowls. It is traditionally eaten in cold weather with Arabic coffee.

title: Khabees (Eastern Arabian saffron-and-cardamom flour pudding)
steps: Heat the water with the sugar, cardamom and saffron until the sugar dissolves, then keep it warm.
In a heavy pan, stir the flour over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes until it darkens slightly and smells toasty.
Pour in the oil or ghee and keep stirring for another few minutes.
Gradually add the warm syrup, stirring constantly so no lumps form, until the mixture thickens and comes together into a smooth, glossy paste.
Stir in the rose water, spread the khabees on a plate and serve warm, traditionally for breakfast around Eid, often with dates or Arabic coffee.

title: Khaliat Nahl (honeycomb cheese-filled bread rolls)

ingredients.name: cream cheese or soft white cheese mixed with a little mozzarella
orange juice or orange blossom water

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm milk and oil and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Cover and leave to double in size, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 20 to 24 small balls. Flatten each ball a little, put a teaspoon of cheese in the middle and pinch it closed.
Place the filled rolls seam-side down, tightly packed together, in a greased round baking tin so they will touch as they rise. Leave to rise for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 C (350 F). Brush the rolls with beaten egg and sprinkle on the seeds.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until deep golden brown.
Warm the honey with the orange juice or blossom water until it is runny and brush it generously over the hot rolls. Serve warm so the cheese is still soft.

title: Saleeg (Hejazi creamy chicken and rice)
steps: Melt half of the butter in a wide heavy pot and soften the onion over medium heat without letting it brown.
Add the chicken, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves and salt, then pour in the water. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, cover and simmer for about 35 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate and keep it warm. Strain the broth if you want it clear, and measure out roughly 700 ml back into the pot.
Add the rice and bring to a boil, then lower the heat and cook, stirring often, until the rice has swallowed most of the liquid.
Pour in the milk a little at a time, stirring, and keep cooking on low heat until the rice is soft and creamy, somewhat like a loose risotto. Add a splash of hot water if it tightens up too much.
Stir in the remaining butter, taste for salt and spoon the rice onto a large platter.
Brown the chicken pieces briefly under a hot grill or in a pan, lay them on top and serve with a spicy tomato salad if you like.

title: Talbina (Arabian barley, milk and honey porridge)

ingredients.name: fine barley flour (or finely ground rolled barley)

steps: Whisk the barley flour with the water in a small saucepan until it is smooth and free of lumps.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it bubbles and begins to thicken, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the milk, lower the heat and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until it is a creamy porridge.
Stir in the salt and honey and cook for one more minute.
Serve warm in bowls with an extra drizzle of honey.

title: Tharid (Meccan bread-and-lamb stew)

ingredients.name: pieces of thin flatbread (pita works), torn into pieces
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides, then add the onion and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, salt and pepper for a minute, then add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and skim. Cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the carrots and zucchini and simmer for another 20 to 25 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the broth has deepened in flavour.
Toast or dry out the torn bread in a low oven for 10 minutes so it holds together better, then spread it over the bottom of a deep serving dish.
Ladle the hot broth over the bread until it is well soaked, then pile the lamb and vegetables on top and serve straight away.
